items.heading: Explains that every emanated and created being is comprised of the four aforementioned discernments of coarseness, which are called Hochma, Bina, Tiferet, and Malchut, in which the upper light expands for the coupling by striking on the screen in Malchut. And their root is the Emanator, called Keter. And since each discernment differs from its fellow, there must be an intermediate discernment between them that includes both discernments. And it contains seven matters: — 1. In every emanated and created being there are four elements, ARMA (fire, wind, water, earth), corresponding to the four letters of the Havaya, which are Hochma, Bina, Tiferet, Malchut, and this is the secret of TaNTA (Taamim, Nekudot, Tagin, Otiot), and of ABYA. 2. And this is the secret of the four discernments in the lower man: 1) his spirituality; 2) the body; 3) the garments; 4) the house he dwells in. And each of them is comprised of four. In his spirituality there is Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya. In his body there is bone, sinew, flesh, skin. In the garments there is tunic, breeches, turban, sash. In the house there is house, courtyard, field, desert. 3. In the four discernments in man there is one discernment that includes them all. And likewise there is an intermediate discernment between every two discernments among them, which includes both. 4. The discernment that includes them all is called the light of Yechida. And it has two discernments: the spark of the Creator, and the spark of the created being. 5. The intermediate discernment between the discernment of spirituality in man, which is NRNHY, and the discernment of the body, is the quarter-log of blood in which Nefesh of Nefesh clothes. And it is found to include the spirituality and the body. 6. The intermediate discernment between the body and the garments is the hair and nails of man. 7. The intermediate discernment between the garments and the house is the tents made of wool and linen. — There is an Emanator and an emanated being. Every emanated being is divided according to the four discernments of coarsening, in which the light expands from the Emanator, to become vessels for the emanated being, and this is the secret of Hochma, Bina, Tiferet, Malchut. And this is the secret of ARMA. And this is the secret of the four letters of the Havaya. And this is the secret of TaNTA. And this is the secret of the four discernments in man: NRNHY, body, garments, the house he dwells in. For there is no emanated being with fewer than four parts.
items.html: *Behold, there is 1an Emanator and an emanated being, 2and the emanated being has in it four elements: fire, wind, water, earth. And they are the four letters of the Havaya, and they are: Hochma, Bina, Tiferet, and Malchut. And behold they are: Taamim, Nekudot, Tagin, Otiot. And they are the same as: Atzilut, Beria, Yetzira, Asiya. Which are the same as the four discernments in man: 1, the inner man, which is the spirituality called: Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya, Yechida. 2, is the body. 3, is the garments upon the body. 4, is the house in which the man, his body, and his garment dwell.

items.heading: And each of the four discernments in man is comprised of four. The spirituality is Haya, Neshama, Ruach, Nefesh. The body is bones, sinews, flesh, skin. The garments are tunic, breeches, turban, sash. The house is house, courtyard, field, desert.
items.html: 3And all these discernments are comprised of four discernments, and they are: the first discernment, of the spirituality, is: 4Neshama of Neshama, and Neshama, Ruach, Nefesh. The second discernment, which is the body, is: the bones, within which is the brain inside, and the sinews, and the flesh, and the skin. As it is written, "skin and flesh have You clothed me, and fenced me with bones and sinews." The third discernment, which are the garments, are known to be the garments required for the common priest: tunic, breeches, turban, and sash. For the four of the High Priest are garments more supernal than these, as mentioned in the Zohar, that these are the garments of the name Adonai, and those are the garments of the name Havaya, but essentially they are only four discernments. The fourth discernment, which is the house, includes: house, courtyard, field, and desert.

items.heading: Between every two discernments there is an intermediate discernment that includes both.
items.html: However, in all these four particular discernments, there is 5one discernment that includes them all, and it is 6intermediate between one discernment and another, including both. An example is what the natural philosophers said, that between the inanimate and the vegetative there is the coral, called Almogim. And between the vegetative and the animate there is the Adnei HaSadeh (the Man of the Field), mentioned in tractate Kilayim, which is like a kind of dog, that grows in the ground, and its navel is rooted in the ground, and it feeds from there, and when its navel is cut it dies. And between the animate and the speaking (human), it is the monkey.

items.heading: Between the Creator and the created being, which is the spirituality in man, there is an intermediate discernment, about which it was said, "You are sons," etc., "you are gods." The Patriarchs are the Chariot.
items.html: And likewise here, between the Creator, blessed be He, 7and the created being, which is the discernment that includes the spirituality, there is an intermediate discernment, about which it was said, "You are sons to the Lord your God," "I said, you are gods," and it is said, "And God went up from over Abraham," and our sages said, 8"The Patriarchs, they are the Chariot."

items.heading: The intermediate discernment is comprised of two sparks: the spark of the Creator, clothed in the spark of the created being, in which are the roots of NRNHY in man.
items.html: And the intent is that there is 9a very small spark, which is the discernment of divinity, drawn 10from the last degree of the Creator, and this 20spark clothes by virtue of another spark, created, which is a very, very fine soul, called Yechida, and in this spark there are 30the roots of the four discernments of spirituality, which are: 40Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya.

items.heading: Between the spirituality in man and the body, there is the discernment of the quarter-log of blood in the Nefesh, which is composed of both. For the Nefesh is spiritual, and the quarter-log of blood, in which the Nefesh clothes, is body.
items.html: And so between the discernment of spirituality and the discernment of the body, there is one discernment that includes both, and it is the discernment of the quarter-log of blood of the Nefesh, for in it is the last spark of the Nefesh, which is the quarter within the Nefesh, meaning, the discernment of 50Nefesh within Nefesh, and therefore it is called "quarter." And this spark clothes in the quarter-log of blood mentioned above, and all is one, as it is written, "for the blood is the Nefesh," said of this quarter-log of blood. And this quarter-log of blood is the most select of all four discernments of the body mentioned above, of which every part is divided into four as above, and it is the first and uppermost quarter of the discernment of the bones of the brains, which is the vitality within it, which is the blood that expands within them to give them life. And in this quarter within the upper blood are included all the roots of the four discernments mentioned above, such that it is the intermediate discernment between the spirituality and the body, and it is composed of both.

items.heading: Between the body and the garments, there is the discernment of the hair and nails of man, which include both. And between the garments and the house, there is an intermediate discernment, which is the tents.
items.html: And so between the second discernment and the third, there is an intermediate discernment, and they are the hair and nails of man, as is known, for this was the garment of Adam HaRishon at first. And behold, they are attached to the skin of man, and resemble the body of man itself. However, upon their removal from there, a garment is made from that hair, in the way that garments are made from the wool of sheep and goats, and the like. And moreover, even while they are attached to the body of man, they resemble a garment, similar to animals and beasts, whose hair is their garment. And the proof of this is Adam HaRishon, regarding the matter of the nails. And we find with Nebuchadnezzar, that this was his garment, as it is written, "till his hair grew like eagles' feathers, and his nails like birds' claws," etc. And so between the discernment of the garments and the discernment of the house, there are the tents, made of wool and linen, which are a discernment of garments, and also serve as a discernment of houses. And this discernment of tents still requires study, whether it is so, or whether there is something else in it.
